correctness.rationale: Every derivation is determined by f=D(t), with N t^(N−1)f=0. Outside characteristic two, the second Leibniz identity and idempotence force 2f²=0, so any nonzero f has valuation at least 2, in contradiction with ff'=f. In characteristic two, D² is a derivation; the same valuation estimate excludes f of valuation at least 2. A unit f forces f'=1, and for valuation 1 the annihilator is (t^(N−1)), which forces f'=1 because the derivative has degree at most N−2. This yields exactly the stated coefficient affine space in each parity. The same argument over residue fields of primes of the coefficient ring identifies the reduced locus, not only its k-points. The h images of the odd powers are independent by their distinct lowest degrees. With a=f(0) the coordinate s=f−a has linear coefficient 1 and D(s)=s+a; rescaling when a≠0 gives the second normal form. This second class can occur only at even length and is distinguished by failure to preserve the maximal ideal. Counting parameters gives the enumerator and orbit sizes. Independently enumerating all coordinate substitutions over F2 and F4 at N=3,4,5,6 confirmed the nonzero orbit sizes (for example, 16 and 48 over F4 at N=6).
residual_risks: Finite reproduction checks conjugacy only in the specified small cases; the general and reduced-locus arguments are algebraic. Nothing is asserted about the nonreduced scheme.

value.rationale: The composition-idempotent condition distinguishes the characteristic-two ordinary toral case from all other characteristics. The result classifies these operators as derivations of the algebra rather than just as projections on its underlying vector space. In particular the two even-length nonzero classes have the same rank but differ by how they act on the maximal ideal, a distinction invisible to the rank enumerator alone. This is a complete classification for the natural arbitrary-length family; no value is claimed for coefficient counting by itself.
residual_risks: No claim about general restricted toral derivations in odd characteristic, multivariate rings, or the unreduced defining scheme.
